citation: Jyoti Srivastava, 'Three Row Houses at East Cullerton', Chicago - Architecture & Cityscape (blog), September 2009: colour photographs of 213, 215 and 217 E. Cullerton Street (East Twentieth Street before the 1930s renaming), c. 2009.
author: Jyoti Srivastava
repository: Chicago - Architecture & Cityscape (blog). Prairie library images a19-jyoti-cullerton-106, a19-jyoti-cullerton-220, a19-jyoti-cullerton-223 and a19-jyoti-cullerton-224 (stream-1900.json).
locator: Photograph 106 (217's east flank and corner oriel, from the north-east, 267 x 400 px); photograph 220 (looking west along the street past 217's east flank and oriel, 400 x 266 px); photograph 223 (217's ground storey on the street: the oriel's copper underside, two round-headed lights and the door, 400 x 266 px).
rights_note: Copyright the photographer ('(c) 2009' on some prints); the Prairie library's ruling is link only. Only what stands in the street and its forms are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-27 (T-3781) from the image store's reference copies (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a19-jyoti-cullerton-106.jpg, -220.jpg, -223.jpg), each about 400 px on its long side.
note: Modern photographs of the surviving house, about 105 years after the scene date: they show its forms, not its 1904 condition. The copper's green patina, the window grilles and the planting are 2009's; the register warns that modern grilles and patina are not proof of the 1904 state.
what_it_supplies: 217's street front: two round-headed lights under the oriel and the door in a carved stone surround west of them (223)
217's corner oriel: a rounded bay sheathed in copper over the ground storey, two storeys tall, its lights bent round it, on a rounded copper underside (106, 220, 223)
217's walls: red brick over a red sandstone base course, stone sills and heads, the ground storey's round-headed openings (106, 220, 223)
a steep gable with a finial over 217's east flank (106)
what_it_does_not_supply: a 1904 date: the photographs are of the surviving house in 2009
the rear, the west flank and the roof behind the gable
dimensions: no scale stands in the frame
